answers.value: The written QA sampling methodology for the underwriting file-review program: the population of bound new-business and renewal files across personal, commercial and specialty lines, the random-plus-targeted stratification logic, and the per-underwriter sample sizes. Scope = one methodology document covering the coming review year.
The review year the methodology governs (e.g. 2026 review cycle, 01-Jan to 31-Dec), with quarterly sampling waves; the prior-year methodology remains the SOR until this version is approved.

Methodology document specifies: base random rate (5% monthly management sample), targeted-risk triggers (new underwriters, authority-exception files, high-hazard classes), stratification by line/authority tier, and minimum 25 files per underwriter per quarter. A missing stratum definition or undefined sample size blocks approval.

Planned sample counts reconcile to the population extract: sum of per-stratum targets equals the total planned reviews, and the random 5% count ties to the bound-policy count in the PAS for each month (delta = 0).

Approved methodology stored in the Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/methodology/ with version v3.x and approval timestamp; superseded versions locked read-only; retained 7 years with underwriting QA records.

Any deviation from the sampling plan (e.g. a stratum with insufficient volume) is logged in Archer with disposition (reduce sample / substitute stratum / defer) and the Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager's rationale.

Methodology cites the internal 'Monthly 5% Sample Review by Underwriting Management' standard and the Internal Audit charter; where files contain filed-rate reviews, references the state filed-rate adherence requirement.
QA methodology and resulting review records retained 7 years per the underwriting file-retention schedule; the approved methodology version is retained for the full period it governs plus 7 years.
Methodology is approved and published before the review-year start (target: by 15-Dec of the preceding year) so Q1 sampling can begin on schedule; no filing to a regulator is required.

Validation population = the full bound-file population the methodology will draw from for the review year, sourced from the PAS bordereau; the methodology's sampling formulas are test-run against this population.

PASS = every line/authority stratum has a defined, statistically defensible sample size, the random rate meets or exceeds the 5% management-review floor, and targeted triggers cover all high-risk categories. FAIL = any stratum unsampled or a sample size below the floor.

If the test-run shows an uncovered stratum or an undersized sample, the methodology is returned to the QA analyst for revision before CUO approval; changes tracked as document revisions with a 5-business-day turnaround.

Acceptance = methodology defines population, stratification, random and targeted criteria, sample sizes and scoring linkage; it is approved by the Chief Underwriting Officer and reproducible from the documented formulas.
Approved methodology and the CUO sign-off record filed in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/methodology/v3.x/.

checklist.step: Embed the monthly 5% management sample as the methodology floor
checklist.value: The random sampling rate is set at or above 5% of monthly bound files per underwriter, matching the Underwriting Management review standard.

checklist.step: Document the stratification and targeting logic
checklist.value: Methodology records how files are stratified by line and authority tier and which risk triggers drive targeted selection.

testing.step: Verify the random rate meets the floor
testing.value: Planned random sample count divided by monthly bound-file count is >= 5% for every underwriter; 0 strata below floor.
Every defined high-risk category (new UW, authority exception, high-hazard class) maps to a targeted-selection rule in the methodology.

checklist.step: Align sampling to file-documentation review objectives
checklist.value: Sampling methodology ensures reviewed files can be scored against file-documentation completeness criteria.

testing.value: Each sampled stratum is tied to the file-documentation scoring checklist; 0 strata without a scoring linkage.

checklist.step: Align methodology with the Internal Audit review cycle
checklist.value: QA sampling methodology is consistent with the annual Internal Audit plan so results are audit-ready.

testing.value: Internal Audit confirms the sampling methodology supports its annual review scope; sign-off recorded before the review year begins.

answers.value: Systemic quality issues surfaced by the QA review cycle (recurring rating errors, form misapplication, authority breaches) that exceed a single-file defect and require management action. Scope = one escalation package per quarter summarising themes across the reviewed population.
The QA cycle that produced the findings (e.g. Q2 2026 review, files bound Apr-Jun 2026); escalation raised within 10 business days of the cycle's defect log closing.

Each escalated issue carries: theme, affected line/team, defect count and rate, root-cause statement (5-whys), estimated exposure, and recommended corrective action. An escalation missing root cause or affected-population size is returned before it is logged.

Escalated defect counts reconcile to the QA defect log for the cycle: the sum of issues rolled into each systemic theme equals the underlying logged defects in Archer (delta = 0); no defect is double-counted across themes.
Escalation memo and supporting analysis stored in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/escalations/<cycle>/ with timestamp and version; management acknowledgement captured; retained 7 years.

Issues management elects not to action are logged with disposition (accept-risk / monitor / defer), owner and rationale in Archer; unresolved systemic themes re-escalate to the CUO at the next cycle with a documented aging note.

Escalation references the internal 'Exceptions Require CUO Approval with Documentation' standard and the QA charter; where a systemic theme touches filed-rate or form compliance, the relevant state requirement is cited.
Escalation records and management responses retained 7 years with the underwriting QA program records.
Escalation delivered within 10 business days of cycle close; no external filing deadline applies as this is an internal management control.

Pre/post: prior-cycle systemic themes are compared to the current cycle to confirm previously escalated issues are trending down after corrective action; a theme that is flat or rising is flagged for stronger intervention.
Each escalated theme is linked to a corrective-action item (CAPA) ticket in Archer with owner and target date; the CAPA reference is recorded on the escalation memo.
Trace population = all systemic themes raised this cycle; each traced end-to-end from underlying QA defects through escalation memo to the assigned CAPA and management decision.

PASS = every systemic theme has documented root cause, quantified impact, a recommended action and a management decision recorded within SLA. FAIL = any theme escalated without root cause or without a logged management response.
Themes with no management response within 10 business days are re-escalated to the Chief Underwriting Officer and logged as an overdue-governance exception in Archer.

Escalation authority follows the QA governance matrix: theme-level issues route to the Underwriting Director/Manager, enterprise or authority-breach themes route to the CUO; the matrix version is cited on the memo.

Acceptance = escalation memo documents each systemic theme with root cause, quantified exposure and recommended action, and a management decision is recorded; evidence stored in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/escalations/<cycle>/ with the CAPA reference.

checklist.step: Route systemic/authority-breach themes to the CUO with documentation
checklist.value: Escalations involving authority exceptions or enterprise exposure are directed to the Chief Underwriting Officer with a documented root cause and recommended action.

testing.value: 100% of authority-breach systemic themes show a documented CUO decision; 0 undocumented escalations.

checklist.step: Feed systemic themes into the Internal Audit review
checklist.value: Escalated themes are shared with Internal Audit to inform the annual audit scope.

testing.value: Each quarter's systemic-issue escalation is provided to Internal Audit; receipt recorded in Archer.

answers.value: Recurring underwriting errors detected across the QA-reviewed file set: rating mistakes, wrong form/edition selection, and guideline/authority deviations. Scope = the aggregated defect data from the current QA cycle, analysed for patterns by line, class, underwriter and error type.
The current QA review cycle (e.g. Q2 2026, files bound Apr-Jun 2026); systemic-pattern analysis runs after the cycle's file scoring is complete.

Each defect record carries error type, line/class, underwriter, authority tier, and financial impact; analysis groups these into patterns. Records with a blank error-type or unmapped line are corrected before pattern detection runs.

Defect counts by pattern reconcile to the total scored-file defect log for the cycle (delta = 0); error rates are computed as defects / files reviewed per stratum and tie back to the sampled population count.

The systemic-error analysis (pivot by error type/line/underwriter, with charts) is stored in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/analysis/<cycle>/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.
Patterns below the materiality threshold are logged as 'monitor' with disposition and rationale; patterns above threshold are logged as systemic findings and routed to the escalation process.
Analysis cites the 'Filed Rates Applied Correctly' and 'File Documentation' internal standards; rating-error patterns reference the applicable filed rate manual/SERFF filing where relevant.
Systemic-error analyses retained 7 years with the QA program records.
Analysis completed in time to feed the quarterly QA report and any escalation, within 10 business days of cycle close; no regulatory filing deadline applies.
Pre/post: current-cycle error patterns are compared to prior cycles to confirm whether previously identified systemic errors have declined after corrective action; persistence or growth is flagged.
Each confirmed systemic pattern is linked to a corrective-action (CAPA) ticket in Archer; the reference is recorded on the analysis workbook.
Analysis population = all scored files in the cycle's QA sample (e.g. ~300-400 files across lines); errors aggregated across the full sample, not a sub-sample.

A pattern is flagged systemic when an error type exceeds the tolerance threshold (e.g. rating errors > 3% of files in a line, or the same guideline deviation on >= 5 files). PASS = all thresholds evaluated and breaches flagged; FAIL = any threshold not evaluated.
Flagged systemic errors are routed to escalation and CAPA; borderline patterns are placed on a watchlist and re-evaluated next cycle with a documented rationale.
Acceptance = systemic error patterns are documented with error type, affected population, rate vs threshold, and root-cause hypothesis, and reviewed by the Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager.
Analysis workbook and findings stored in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/analysis/<cycle>/.

Materiality/tolerance thresholds: an error type is systemic when it exceeds 3% of files in a line-of-business stratum or recurs on 5+ files with the same root cause; financial-impact materiality set at $10,000 aggregate per pattern. Thresholds documented in the QA methodology and applied uniformly across strata.

checklist.step: Classify defects against file-documentation criteria
checklist.value: Each detected error is mapped to a file-documentation standard element so systemic gaps in documentation are visible.

testing.value: 100% of logged defects carry a documentation-criterion mapping; 0 unclassified defects enter the pattern analysis.

checklist.step: Isolate filed-rate application errors
checklist.value: Rating-error patterns are tested against the filed rate manual to confirm whether filed rates were applied correctly.

testing.step: Re-derive a sample of flagged rating errors
testing.value: For flagged rating-error files, the re-derived premium confirms the error; 0 false positives in the systemic count.

checklist.step: Use peer review to confirm systemic findings
checklist.value: A second QA reviewer or the QA manager peer-reviews the pattern analysis before a finding is declared systemic.

testing.value: Every systemic finding carries a documented peer/manager review; 0 findings issued without a second reviewer.

answers.value: The quarterly Underwriting QA report: quality scores, defect rates and trends by line/team/underwriter, systemic themes, and improvement recommendations. Scope = one report covering the completed quarter's QA cycle across all lines.
The completed quarter (e.g. Q2 2026), with rolling four-quarter trend context; report issued within 15 business days of quarter close.

Report includes: files reviewed, defect count and rate, score distribution, top defect categories, systemic themes, CAPA status and recommendations. A section with a blank metric or a missing prior-quarter comparator is completed before issuance.
Report totals reconcile to the QA defect log and Power BI dataset: files-reviewed and defect counts in the report equal the Archer QA source counts for the quarter (delta = 0).
Final report (PDF + Power BI dashboard snapshot) stored in SharePoint /UW-Quality/reports/<quarter>/ with version and issue timestamp; distribution list recorded; retained 7 years.
Data anomalies found during report prep (e.g. a stratum with unexpectedly low review coverage) are logged with disposition (restate / footnote / defer) and rationale before the report is signed off.
Scoring model and trend calculations use the approved QA scoring rubric version in force for the quarter; a change in rubric version is footnoted so trends remain comparable.
Trend sensitivity: quarter-over-quarter score changes are recomputed excluding new-underwriter files to confirm movements are not driven by sample-mix; material mix effects are disclosed.
Materiality: a quarter-over-quarter defect-rate change above 2 percentage points, or any new systemic theme, must be narrated in the report.
Report references the QA program charter and the 'Monthly 5% Sample Review by Underwriting Management' and 'Annual Audit by Internal Audit' internal standards it evidences.
Quarterly QA reports retained 7 years with the underwriting QA program records.
Report issued within 15 business days of quarter close per the QA governance calendar; no external regulatory filing deadline.
Inspection population = the issued quarterly report and its supporting Power BI dataset; every metric and chart is inspected against source data before sign-off.

PASS = all metrics tie to source, prior-quarter comparators present, systemic themes and recommendations included, and CUO sign-off obtained. FAIL = any untied metric, missing comparator, or absent recommendation section.
A metric that fails to reconcile blocks issuance; the figure is traced back to Archer/Power BI, corrected and re-reconciled before the report is released.

Field definitions sourced from the QA data dictionary: files_reviewed, defect_count, defect_rate, score, line_of_business, authority_tier, quarter - one row per reviewed file feeding the report aggregates.
Source control total = Archer QA reviewed-file and defect counts for the quarter; the Power BI report totals reconcile to these with 0 variance.

In-scope period/effective dates: the completed calendar quarter under report (e.g. 01-Apr-2026 to 30-Jun-2026 for Q2), with the prior four quarters included only as trend comparators; files bound outside the quarter are excluded from the headline metrics.

checklist.step: Report the management sample results
checklist.value: The quarterly report presents the 5% management-sample review results and defect rates by underwriter and line.

testing.value: Report shows the achieved sample rate met or exceeded 5% for the quarter; shortfalls are explained.

checklist.step: Provide QA results to support Internal Audit
checklist.value: The quarterly report is packaged so Internal Audit can rely on it for the annual audit.

testing.value: Report includes methodology reference, population, and reconciliations; Internal Audit accepts it without rework.

answers.value: The selected bound files under QA review, scored against the underwriting guideline checklist covering rate adequacy, form/edition selection and authority compliance. Scope = the sampled files for the current cycle, scored one file at a time in the QA scorecard.
The current QA review cycle (e.g. Q2 2026, files bound Apr-Jun 2026); only files bound in-cycle are scored.

For each file the scorecard captures: rate applied vs filed rate, form/edition used, authority tier vs signer, referral evidence and documentation completeness. A file missing the bound premium, form record or signer identity cannot be scored and is returned for data completion.
Count of scored files reconciles to the selected sample (delta = 0); each scored file's rate figure ties to the PAS/rating record and the assigned score rolls up to the cycle scorecard totals.
Completed scorecards (one per file) stored in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/scores/<cycle>/ with reviewer, timestamp and version; retained 7 years.
Files scoring below the pass threshold or with a critical error (rate error, unauthorized bind) are logged as defects with disposition (coach / correct / escalate) and routed to the defect log.
Scoring uses the approved QA guideline-checklist/rubric version in force for the cycle; the rubric version is stamped on each scorecard so scores are comparable across reviewers.
Scoring sensitivity checked via calibration: a subset of files is independently re-scored by a Senior Underwriter; score dispersion beyond +/-1 rubric point triggers reviewer recalibration.
Materiality: any rate-adequacy error, form misapplication affecting coverage, or authority breach is a critical (fail) defect regardless of overall score; documentation nits are non-critical.

Scorecard cites the 'Filed Rates Applied Correctly', 'Clear Authority Levels by Premium, Limit, and Line of Business' and 'File Documentation' internal standards, plus the filed rate manual for rate-adequacy checks.
File scores and supporting evidence retained 7 years with the QA program records.
Scoring completed within the cycle window so defect logs and the quarterly report can be produced on schedule; no external filing deadline.
Test population = all files in the cycle's selected sample (e.g. 25 files per underwriter per quarter across lines); every sampled file is scored, none skipped.
PASS = file score >= threshold (e.g. 90%) with no critical error; FAIL = score below threshold or any critical error (rate adequacy, form, authority). Rate applied must match filed rate to the cent.
Failed files generate a defect record and coaching/correction action; disputed scores are adjudicated by the Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager with the rationale recorded.
Acceptance = every sampled file has a completed scorecard covering rate adequacy, form selection and authority compliance, with a recorded pass/fail and defects logged for failures.
Scorecards and evidence stored in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/scores/<cycle>/.

Approved methodology/model version: QA guideline-checklist rubric v3.x and the filed rate manual / SERFF filing effective on each file's policy date; rate parameters are sourced from the filed rate tables loaded in the PAS/Earnix, never manually keyed.

Applicable citation: the state filed-rate adherence requirement and internal authority matrix v3.2; rate-adequacy and authority-compliance scoring is anchored to the filed rate and the approved authority levels for each line and state.

checklist.step: Score every file against documentation criteria
checklist.value: Each bound file is scored for required documentation (submission, rating worksheet, referral evidence, signer) per the file-documentation standard.

testing.value: 100% of sampled files have a documentation score; missing-doc files logged as defects.

checklist.step: Check filed-rate application on each file
checklist.value: The premium of record is compared to the filed rate manual for the class/state; deviations without an approved basis are scored as critical defects.

testing.value: Re-performed premium equals the filed value to the cent for passing files; 0 unexplained rate variances.

checklist.step: Verify authority compliance on each file
checklist.value: The binding underwriter's authority tier (premium, limit, line) is checked against the signed exposure; over-authority binds are critical defects.

testing.value: 100% of sampled files show the bind was within the signer's authority or carried a documented referral/approval; 0 unauthorized binds unflagged.

answers.value: QA findings from the scored files, scored for severity and recorded as defects in the QA defect log. Scope = all findings raised during the current cycle's file scoring, each logged as a discrete defect with severity and category.
The current QA review cycle (e.g. Q2 2026); defects are logged as files are scored and the log is closed at cycle end.

Each defect record carries: file/policy number, error category, severity (critical/major/minor), rubric criterion breached, underwriter, and recommended action. A defect missing severity or category cannot be saved.
Logged defect count reconciles to the failed criteria across all scorecards for the cycle (delta = 0); each defect links to exactly one source scorecard so counts cannot double.
Defect log exported and stored in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/defects/<cycle>/ with timestamp and version; each defect retains its source scorecard link; retained 7 years.
Contested or unclear defects are logged with disposition (confirm / downgrade / withdraw) after review; withdrawn defects retain a rationale and are excluded from rate calculations.
Each defect traces to the source file screens/documents: the PAS policy record and the stored rating worksheet/scorecard that evidence the error, linked from the Archer defect record.
Defect status fields follow the QA workflow: Open -> In Review -> Confirmed -> Actioned -> Closed; no defect is Closed without an action or an approved withdrawal.
Date fields (found date, review date, closed date) are populated and ordered; found date must equal or precede review and close dates, matching the cycle timeline.
Defect log references the QA scoring rubric and the 'File Documentation' and 'Peer Review' internal standards; rating defects cite the filed rate manual.
Defect log and linked scorecards retained 7 years with the QA program records.
Defect log finalised at cycle close so it can feed the quarterly report and CAPA; no external filing deadline applies.
Test population = all findings from the cycle's scored files; every finding is scored for severity and logged, with a reconciliation to the scorecards.

PASS = every finding logged with severity, category, source link and action, and log count ties to scorecard failures. FAIL = any finding unlogged, missing severity, or lacking a source-scorecard link.
Findings that cannot be substantiated are withdrawn with rationale by the QA manager; unresolved severity disputes escalate to the Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager for final scoring.
Acceptance = all QA findings scored and logged as defects in Archer with severity, category, source link and recommended action; log reconciled to the scorecards.
Defect log and evidence stored in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/defects/<cycle>/.

Approved methodology/model version: the QA severity rubric v3.x (critical/major/minor definitions) in force for the cycle; severity parameters are sourced from the approved QA methodology, not set ad hoc per reviewer.

Source-system field definitions from the QA data dictionary (policy_number, error_category, severity, criterion, underwriter, found_date); control total = count of failed rubric criteria across all cycle scorecards, which must equal the logged defect count with 0 variance.

checklist.step: Log documentation defects against the standard
checklist.value: File-documentation failures are recorded as defects with the specific documentation element that was missing or deficient.

testing.value: 100% of documentation defects cite a file-documentation criterion; 0 uncategorised defects.

checklist.step: Peer-review contested defects before closing
checklist.value: Contested or critical defects are peer-reviewed by the QA manager before final scoring.

testing.step: Confirm peer review on critical defects
testing.value: Every critical defect has a documented second review; 0 unilateral critical scores.

checklist.step: Aggregate defects to management sample metrics
checklist.value: Defect scoring rolls up to the 5% management-sample defect-rate metrics reported to underwriting management.

testing.value: Defect count / files reviewed reconciles to the management-sample metric; 0 reconciliation variance.

answers.value: The risk-stratified sample of bound files drawn for the QA review cycle. Scope = a sample selected from the full bound-file population, stratified by line, authority tier and risk triggers, sized per the approved QA methodology.
The QA cycle being sampled (e.g. Q2 2026, files bound Apr-Jun 2026); the sampling frame is the population of policies bound in that window.

The population extract carries policy number, line, class, state, premium, bind date, authority tier and underwriter; records missing line, premium or underwriter are corrected before stratification so no file is mis-binned.
The sampling frame count reconciles to the PAS bound-policy count for the period (delta = 0); selected sample counts by stratum equal the methodology's planned targets and sum to the total draw.

The population extract, the seeded random-selection log and the final sample list are stored in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/samples/<cycle>/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.
Strata that cannot meet the planned sample size (low volume) are logged with disposition (census the stratum / reduce target / substitute) and the QA manager's rationale in Archer.
Each selected file traces to its PAS policy record and source screens so reviewers can retrieve the file; the sample list stores the PAS policy key for every drawn file.
Policy status of sampled files aligns to workflow: only Bound/Issued policies are eligible; quoted-not-bound or cancelled-flat records are excluded from the frame.
Bind/effective dates on sampled files fall within the cycle window; files with dates outside the period are removed from the frame before selection.
Sample plan cites the approved QA sampling methodology and the 'Monthly 5% Sample Review by Underwriting Management' and 'Annual Audit by Internal Audit' internal standards.
Sampling records (frame, selection log, sample list) retained 7 years with the QA program records.
Sample drawn at cycle start so scoring can complete within the cycle window; no external filing deadline applies.
Pre/post: the drawn sample's line/authority mix is compared to the population mix to confirm the stratified sample is representative and risk-weighted, not skewed; material skew triggers a re-draw.
The sampling run is recorded as a QA cycle task in Archer with the seed value and parameters, so the selection is reproducible; the run reference is stored on the sample list.
Selection population = all in-scope bound files for the period; the risk-stratified draw (random 5% floor plus targeted high-risk files) is validated against this frame.

PASS = every stratum meets its planned sample size (or is documented as a census/exception), the random floor >= 5% is met, and all targeted triggers are represented. FAIL = any stratum under target without a logged exception.
If a stratum is undersampled, the QA analyst substitutes or censuses per the methodology; unresolved gaps are escalated to the Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager before scoring starts.
Acceptance = a reproducible, risk-stratified sample list that meets the methodology's per-stratum sizes and random floor, with the selection log retained.
Frame, selection log and sample list stored in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/samples/<cycle>/.

Source-system field definitions from the PAS/QA data dictionary (policy_number, line_of_business, class, state, premium, bind_date, authority_tier, underwriter); control total = PAS bound-policy count for the period, which must equal the sampling frame count with 0 variance before selection.

checklist.step: Meet the 5% management-sample floor in selection
checklist.value: The random component of the draw is at or above 5% of monthly bound files per underwriter.

testing.value: Random selections / bound files >= 5% for every underwriter in the sample; 0 shortfalls without a logged exception.

checklist.step: Draw a sample that supports the annual audit
checklist.value: Sampling is risk-stratified and reproducible so Internal Audit can rely on the QA results.

testing.value: Re-running the documented selection with the stored seed reproduces the same sample; 0 differences.

answers.value: Pricing/rate-application accuracy on the sampled bound files: whether the filed rate, rating variables, tier/territory factors and schedule/experience mods were applied correctly. Scope = the QA sample files, validated one file at a time by re-deriving premium.
The current QA cycle (e.g. Q2 2026, files bound Apr-Jun 2026); the filed rate version in effect on each file's policy date is used for re-derivation.

For each file the rating inputs are checked as populated and valid: class code, exposure base, state/territory, tier, mods and filed factors. A blank class code, territory or filed factor halts validation for that file until sourced from the rating record.

The QA re-derived premium reconciles to the bound premium of record to the cent (delta = 0 for a pass); any variance is quantified and attributed to a specific rating step (wrong factor, mis-keyed exposure, superseded rate version).

Per-file validation worksheets (system premium vs re-derived premium, with the variance cause) stored in Archer QA module and SharePoint /UW-Quality/rate-validation/<cycle>/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.

Files with a rate variance are logged as rating defects with disposition (correct endorsement / refer for deviation approval / coach) and severity; premium-impacting errors are flagged critical and routed to the defect log.

Validation cites the 'Filed Rates Applied Correctly', 'Deviation from Filed Rates per Authority Matrix' and 'Mandatory Pricing Tool Usage' internal standards, and the filed rate manual / SERFF filing for each class and state.
Rate-validation worksheets and defects retained 7 years with the QA program records.
Validation completed within the cycle window so rate defects feed the quarterly report and any deviation follow-up; no external filing deadline applies.

checklist.step: Re-derive premium against the filed rate
checklist.value: For each sampled file, premium is recomputed from the filed rate manual/SERFF filing effective on the policy date and compared to the bound premium.

checklist.step: Attribute any variance to a rating step
checklist.value: Variances are traced to a specific cause (factor, exposure, tier, mod, rate version) and recorded on the validation worksheet.

testing.step: Confirm filed-rate accuracy on the sample
testing.value: Re-derived premium equals the bound premium to the cent for passing files; 0 unexplained variances.
Rating-error rate = files with premium variance / files validated, reported by line; premium-impacting errors flagged critical.

checklist.step: Verify deviations follow the authority matrix
checklist.value: Any departure from filed rates is checked for a documented approval per authority matrix v3.2.

testing.value: 100% of rate deviations in the sample carry an approval at the required authority level; 0 unauthorised deviations.

checklist.step: Confirm rating was done in the mandated tool
checklist.value: The premium of record originates from Earnix/PAS rating (rating session present), not an off-system calculation.

testing.step: Verify tool usage on sampled files
testing.value: Every sampled file shows a rating session ID from the mandated tool; 0 off-system prices.

answers.value: Underwriter competency gaps derived from QA scores, Internal Audit findings and performance data, assessed per underwriter and per competency (rate application, referral discipline, documentation, appetite adherence). Scope = the underwriting team under development for the period.
The assessment period (e.g. H1 2026), aggregating the two most recent QA cycles plus current-year audit findings and performance metrics.

Each underwriter's record carries QA score trend, defect categories, authority tier, tenure and any audit findings, mapped to the competency framework. A record missing QA data or competency mapping is completed before a gap is concluded.

Competency inputs reconcile to source: QA scores tie to the defect log, audit findings tie to the Internal Audit register, and each underwriter's file counts match the PAS (delta = 0) so gaps are grounded in complete data.

Gap assessment (per-underwriter competency matrix and development recommendations) stored in Archer/SharePoint /UW-Quality/competency/<period>/ with timestamp and version; access restricted to management/training; retained 7 years.
Where data is insufficient to assess a competency (e.g. new underwriter, low file volume), it is logged as 'insufficient data - monitor' with rationale rather than scored as a gap.
Assessment references the 'Authority Tied to Competency' and 'Technical Training by Line of Business' internal standards that competency development supports.
Competency assessments and development plans retained 7 years with the underwriting training/QA records, subject to HR data-handling controls.
Gap assessment completed ahead of the training-plan cycle so development actions can be scheduled; no external filing deadline applies.
Assessment population = all underwriters with at least the minimum QA-reviewed file volume for the period; each is assessed against the full competency framework.

A competency is a gap when the underwriter's metric falls below the framework standard (e.g. QA score < 90%, repeat defect category, or an audit finding). PASS = every in-scope underwriter assessed on all competencies with evidence; FAIL = any underwriter unassessed or a gap concluded without data.
Confirmed gaps route to individual development plans; disputed assessments are reviewed with the Underwriting Director/Manager and the rationale recorded before finalisation.
Acceptance = a documented per-underwriter competency matrix grounded in QA/audit/performance data, with identified gaps and recommended development actions.
Competency matrix and development recommendations stored in Archer/SharePoint /UW-Quality/competency/<period>/.

Source-system field definitions from the QA/HR data dictionary (underwriter_id, qa_score, defect_category, audit_finding, authority_tier, tenure, competency); control totals = QA defect-log and Internal Audit register counts per underwriter, which must reconcile to the competency inputs with 0 variance.

Applicable citation: the internal 'Authority Tied to Competency' standard - underwriting authority is granted and retained only where competency is demonstrated; assessments feed authority-progression decisions. No external regulatory rule governs this internal HR/QA process.

checklist.step: Tie competency assessment to authority
checklist.value: Competency gaps are assessed against the authority tier each underwriter holds so authority remains tied to demonstrated competency.

testing.value: Every underwriter whose competency falls below standard for their tier is flagged for development or authority review; 0 unaddressed misalignments.

checklist.step: Map gaps to line-of-business technical training
checklist.value: Identified gaps are mapped to the technical-training curriculum for the relevant line of business.

testing.value: 100% of identified gaps have a mapped technical-training action; 0 gaps without a development path.

answers.value: Underwriter readiness for increased underwriting authority (higher premium/limit/line-of-business limits), assessed against QA performance, competency and experience criteria. Scope = the underwriters proposed for an authority increase this review round.
The authority-review round (e.g. mid-year 2026), using trailing QA cycles and current-year performance and audit data for each candidate.

Each candidate's assessment carries current authority tier, requested tier, QA score trend, defect history, referral compliance and tenure. A candidate record missing QA data or the requested tier cannot be assessed.
Candidate metrics reconcile to source: QA scores tie to the defect log and file counts tie to the PAS (delta = 0); the authority matrix thresholds applied match the approved authority matrix v3.2.

Assessment forms and outcomes (approve / hold / decline with conditions) stored in the underwriting workstation and SharePoint /UW-Quality/authority/<round>/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.
Candidates not meeting criteria are logged with disposition (defer with development plan / conditional increase / decline) and rationale; conditional grants carry documented monitoring requirements.
Assessment cites the 'Authority Tied to Competency' and 'Clear Authority Levels by Premium, Limit, and Line of Business' internal standards and the authority matrix v3.2.
Authority-progression assessments and CUO approvals retained 7 years with the underwriting authority records.
Assessments completed and approved before the authority-grant effective date; the updated authority register takes effect only after CUO sign-off. No external filing deadline applies.

Pre/post: the candidate's authority tier before and after is compared, and the first QA cycle after a grant is reviewed to confirm performance holds at the higher authority; regressions trigger authority review.
Each approved authority change is recorded as an entry in the underwriting authority register with the CUO approval reference; the register update ID is stored on the assessment form.
Test population = all candidates put forward for an authority increase this round; each is assessed against every readiness criterion.

PASS = candidate meets QA-score, defect-history, referral-compliance and tenure thresholds for the requested tier and is approved by the CUO. FAIL = any threshold unmet without documented conditions, or an increase granted without CUO sign-off.
Candidates who fall short are deferred with a development plan or granted a conditional/partial increase with monitoring; exceptions require CUO approval with documentation.
Acceptance = each candidate has a documented readiness assessment against defined criteria, a recorded outcome, and CUO sign-off for any authority increase before it takes effect.
Assessment forms, outcomes and CUO approvals stored in the underwriting workstation and SharePoint /UW-Quality/authority/<round>/.

checklist.step: Grant authority only on demonstrated competency
checklist.value: An authority increase is recommended only where QA performance and competency criteria for the requested tier are met.

testing.value: 100% of approved increases show documented competency evidence meeting the tier thresholds; 0 grants without evidence.

checklist.step: Assess against the clear authority levels
checklist.value: Requested authority is evaluated against the documented authority levels by premium, limit and line of business.

testing.value: Every approved change updates the authority register to the exact premium/limit/line granted; 0 register mismatches.

answers.value: Post-training knowledge assessments administered to underwriters after each training module (e.g. new rate filing, appetite change, line-specific technical training). Scope = the cohort that completed the training event, assessed against the module's learning objectives.
The training delivery window (e.g. the June 2026 technical-training series); assessments administered within 5 business days of each module's delivery.
Each assessment record carries participant, module, score, pass/fail and date. A record missing the participant or module cannot be saved; unanswered questions are scored as incorrect, not blank.
Assessment completion reconciles to the training attendance list: every attendee has an assessment record (delta = 0); non-completers are followed up rather than dropped from the count.
Assessment results and answer keys stored in SharePoint /UW-Quality/training/<module>/ and the training log in Archer, with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.
Participants below the pass mark are logged with disposition (retake / targeted coaching / re-training) and the follow-up date; repeated failures feed the competency-gap assessment.
Assessments reference the '40 Hours of Continuing Education Annually' and 'Technical Training by Line of Business' internal standards that the training program satisfies.
Training and assessment records retained 7 years with the underwriting training records to evidence continuing-education compliance.
Assessments administered within 5 business days of delivery and results logged to update each underwriter's CE hours; no external filing deadline applies.
Pre/post: where a pre-training baseline quiz was given, post-training scores are compared to confirm knowledge gain; modules with no measurable gain are flagged for redesign.
Each assessment cycle is recorded as a training-log entry in Archer linked to the module and cohort; the log ID is stored on the results file.
Test population = all underwriters who attended the training module; every attendee is assessed, with non-completers tracked to closure.
PASS = participant scores at or above the pass mark (e.g. 80%); FAIL = below the pass mark. Cohort-level target: >= 90% first-time pass rate, else the module content/delivery is reviewed.
Failing participants are scheduled for a retake or coaching; unresolved failures escalate to the Underwriting Director/Manager and feed the competency-gap assessment.
Acceptance = every attendee has a scored assessment tied to the module objectives, results logged, and follow-up recorded for any failures.
Assessment results and follow-ups stored in SharePoint /UW-Quality/training/<module>/ and the Archer training log.

Approved methodology/model version: the module's assessment blueprint and answer key (version-controlled) mapped to the stated learning objectives; the pass mark and scoring rules are sourced from the approved training standard, not set per session.

checklist.step: Credit assessed training to CE hours
checklist.value: Passed post-training assessments credit the underwriter's continuing-education hours toward the 40-hour annual requirement.

testing.value: Each passing participant's CE record is updated with the module hours; year-to-date totals track toward 40 hours.

checklist.step: Assess against line-of-business technical content
checklist.value: Assessments test the line-specific technical content delivered, confirming competency by line of business.

testing.value: Every learning objective maps to at least one assessment item; 0 objectives untested.

answers.value: A case-based calibration workshop where underwriters independently assess the same anonymised case files and then align on the correct decision, rating and referral. Scope = one workshop session with a defined cohort and a set of curated calibration cases.
The scheduled workshop date within the current training cycle (e.g. a Q3 2026 calibration session); cases are drawn from recent QA-reviewed files anonymised for training.

The workshop pack carries: curated cases with a facilitator answer key, the calibration scoring sheet, attendee roster and a decision-variance capture form. A session without an answer key or roster is not run.
Attendance reconciles to the invited cohort (delta = 0 or documented absences); each attendee submits a decision on every case so the count of responses equals attendees x cases.

Workshop materials, attendance record and the calibration variance analysis stored in SharePoint /UW-Quality/calibration/<date>/ and the Archer training log, with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.
Cases with high decision variance across attendees are logged as calibration gaps with disposition (guideline clarification / follow-up training / referral-trigger update) and owner.

checklist.step: Calibrate on line-of-business technical cases
checklist.value: Workshop cases are drawn from the relevant lines of business so calibration reinforces line-specific technical standards.

testing.value: Post-calibration decision variance across attendees narrows to within one tier/decision band on the case set; residual gaps logged for follow-up.

checklist.step: Credit workshop attendance to CE hours
checklist.value: Workshop attendance is logged and credited toward the 40-hour annual continuing-education requirement.

testing.value: Every attendee's CE record is updated with the workshop hours; attendance roster reconciles to the credited list.

checklist.step: Use peer discussion to align on the correct decision
checklist.value: Attendees peer-review each other's case decisions and converge on the guideline-correct outcome with the facilitator's key.

testing.value: Each case ends with a documented consensus decision and rationale; 0 cases left unresolved.
